question.text: Consider a quadratic equation \(a x^2+2 b x+c=0\) where \(a, b, c\) are positive real numbers. If the equation has no real root, then which of the following is true?

options.text: a, b, c cannot be in A.P. or H.P. but can be in G.P.
a, b, c cannot be in G.P. or H.P. but can be in A.P.
\(a, b, c\) cannot be in A.P. or G.P. but can be in H.P.
a, b, c cannot be in A.P., G.P. or H.P.

solution.text:
Hint : For no real root
\(\begin{aligned}
& (2 b)^2-4 a c  < 0 \\
& b^2 < a c \\
& b < \sqrt{a c} \because a, b, c > 0
\end{aligned}\)
If in \(A P\), then \(a+c=2 b\)
i.e., \(\mathrm{x}=-1\) a solution
\(\begin{aligned}
& \therefore a, b, c \text { not in AP } \\
& \because b^2 < a c
\end{aligned}\)
\(\therefore a, b, c\) not in GP
For HP \(\quad b=\frac{2 a c}{a+c}=\frac{2 \sqrt{a c}}{\sqrt{\frac{a}{c}}+\sqrt{\frac{c}{a}}}\)
\(\sqrt{\frac{a}{c}}+\sqrt{\frac{c}{a}} \geq 2\)
\(\therefore \frac{2 \sqrt{a c}}{\sqrt{\frac{a}{c}}+\sqrt{\frac{c}{a}}} \leq 2 \therefore a, b, c\) in HP is possible
